Ozaryntsi Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Ozaryntsi's Jewish community, believed present from the 15th century, developed a rich religious infrastructure — a Hasidic court by 1863 and three synagogues by the turn of the 20th century — before enduring six separate pogroms between 1919 and 1920 alone. Under German and Romanian occupation from July 1941, some of the first Jews killed were burned alive rather than shot; a ghetto later held the local community alongside roughly 2,000 deportees from Bessarabia and Bukovina, most of whom died of disease and starvation, leaving only 87 survivors by September 1943. By 1970, only 5 Jews remained in Ozaryntsi.
